page: Amazon Web Services c6id.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via hyperthreading on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512, AVX512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache. Memory resources total 128.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a compute-centric 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided through bundled NVMe SSD instance storage totaling 3,800 GB, and networking performance offers a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps without GPU acceleration.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct strengths in parallel computation and multi-threaded throughput. Multi-core testing exhibits upper-tier execution, scoring 61,944.02 in stress-ng multi-core and 57,561.79 in PassMark CPU tests. The instance also shows strong results in PassMark encryption (56,252.89), extended instructions (53,508.67), and Clang software compilation (41,593.0). Conversely, single-core metrics fall into middle-tier bands, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1,689.0 and stress-ng single-core scoring 1,893.99. Memory bandwidth tests yield mid-tier numbers, measuring 165.54 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 66.11 GB/sec for uncached writes.

The 3,800 GB NVMe local storage paired with strong database operations (26,275.83 in PassMark) and static web serving throughput of 45.17 GB/sec makes this server operationally effective for data-intensive I/O pipelines. However, because local NVMe instance store volumes are ephemeral, workloads requiring long-term data durability must implement independent replication or snapshot tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high ratio of vCPUs to memory targets compute-dense scaling rather than memory-heavy in-memory engines. It is appropriate for batch processing, CI/CD build farms, media rendering, static web tiers, and intermediate caching layers that require local, high-speed NVMe scratch storage alongside extensive thread concurrency.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 3.5 GHz, it includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM and 3,800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, alongside 25 Gbps baseline networking. The instance shows top-tier throughput in multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core (61,944.02), PassMark CPU (57,561.79), and Clang compilation (41,593.0), while single-thread and memory bandwidth figures place in median performance bands. With its balanced 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio and fast local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as distributed CI/CD compilation, video transcoding, static web serving, and high-throughput data processing that benefits from local scratch space.
